newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel steadier, but no confidence till next wee.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel steadier, but no confidence till next wee.

text.p: NWE cracked fuel oil was broadly stable on Friday, despite firmer crude futures.
"The confidence has gone. I think we will have to wait until next week before people accept that crude has picked up," said one European trader.
Other dealers were also cautiously optimistic there might be a marginal recovery in prices "I know crude came off, but fuel really dumped, too much I think," said a dealer at a major.
High sulphur barges bucked the generally stable trend by kicking up $4-5 a tonne or so. Activity in the barge market was moderate for a Friday and trades were heard around $120 fob ARA.
Cargo business was essentially restricted to talk and paper trades. "There's still nothing fundamental to suggest that $115 (cif NWE) is off the market," said one trader.

The low sulphur market looked bruised, but not beaten. Support may come next week from Turkey's 1.5 percent tender that was awarded to two traders and a short into the Med. But the main Med buyer remained relaxed and looking at January barrels, not December. Much will depend upon the eventual destination of the 45-50kt end Dec cargo which has been joined on the market by a 20kt parcel. Prices were close to swaps at around $129 fob NWE. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 8980
